summary: It's the same simple hot-potato press-your-luck game as base Exploding Kittens, but scaled up to fit huge groups with a bigger deck and sillier extra cards. Turns are quick and the humor is broad and juvenile, so it plays best as a loud, casual icebreaker rather than a game with real strategic depth.
praised: Easy to teach to non-gamers and kids in minutes
Great for large groups (up to 10 players) where few games scale
Quick, high-energy rounds with real tension when drawing
Irreverent NSFW-adjacent art and humor lands well with casual/party crowds
criticised: Very light, mostly luck-driven with limited meaningful decisions
Player elimination means knocked-out players sit out and wait
Humor and card art can feel gimmicky or wear thin after repeated plays
Little replayability or depth for regular gamer groups

scoring.why: The winner is simply the last player who hasn't drawn an Exploding Kitten
